name: The Sacred Cedar of Kirishima Jingu

location.address: 霧島神宮, 鹿児島県霧島市霧島田口2608-5 (Kirishima Jingu, Kirishima)

access: Free, shrine precinct; the tree stands fenced in the front courtyard, right of the approach to the main hall, visible from the open ground around it.
transport: Day trip. JR Nippo line to Kirishima-Jingu station, then Kagoshima Kotsu bus toward Kirishima Iwasaki Hotel, about 15 minutes (ja.wikipedia). Total from Kagoshima city centre NOT verified; train time and timetable not checked, expect roughly 1.5 to 2 hours each way.

photo_hint.own: Hidde photograph, sighting 0ee5b139-7042-4bcb-a109-4e8b8d051174, approved for use uncredited
photo_hint.open_licence: File:霧島神宮（御神木）.jpg, CC BY-SA 4.0, author 矢野弘幸, own work 2018-09-10, geotag 31.858311,130.8712, viewed: same tree (fern patch on trunk, shimenawa, fence), tight crop and low res, so Hidde's is better

recognise: The single huge cedar inside a low wooden fence in the front courtyard, right of the approach to the main hall, a rope with paper streamers (shimenawa) tied round the foot of the trunk and a small wooden notice board at the fence.
verify_notes: Shrine's own tourist-association page (kirishima-sjc.or.jp) and pmiyazaki.com (shrine guide): estimated about 800 years, height 38.2 m, trunk girth 6.8 m. Called 霧島杉 / 霧島メアサ; said to be the ancestor of southern Kyushu cedars (ja.wikipedia, 'estimated about 800 years'). pmiyazaki: it was already standing before the shrine was re-established on the present site in 1484 (page's wording 'transplanted to this location' is about the shrine, not necessarily the tree; do not say the tree was moved). It had declined and leaned about 10 degrees; restoration work April 2013 (pmiyazaki). Sources do not say how the figures were measured (girth height not given), so 6.8 m is a source figure, girth_cm 680. DESIGNATION: none found. ja.wikipedia does not list it as a natural monument or giant-tree entry; I did not find it on a Kagoshima prefectural or Environment Ministry list, so do not call it designated. Age is source-given, repeated as 'about 800'; age_min/max band is mine, broad. PIN: OSM natural=tree node 13863502742 at 31.858319,130.871140 and the Commons geotag (31.858311,130.8712) agree within 5 m; Hidde's phone fix 31.858505,130.871308 is about 26 m NE, consistent with him standing back from a 38 m tree; his photo shows the same fenced tree. Pin = OSM node, confirmed. ALIVE: Hidde's photograph 2026-10-02 shows a healthy crown; also lifecheck RECENT nearby iNat records. Shrine is Kirishima Jingu in Kirishima city, Kagoshima Prefecture (pmiyazaki's page header says Miyazaki; that is the site name only). Shrine coordinates 31.858944,130.871861 (ja.wikipedia). Day-trip boundary: well beyond 30 min of the centre, label as Kirishima, true time not verified.
story:
Every cedar in southern Kyushu is said to descend from this one. Kirishima Jingu calls its sacred tree the Kirishima-sugi, or Kirishima measa, the ancestor of the region's cedars, and that claim is tradition rather than anything a laboratory has tested.

The size is easier to check. The shrine's tourist association gives it 38.2 metres of height, 6.8 metres round the trunk and an age of about 800 years. Nobody publishes how those figures were taken, so read the age as the shrine's estimate rather than a count of rings.

If the estimate holds, the cedar was here before the shrine was. Kirishima Jingu was re-established on its present site in 1484, and the shrine's own guide says this tree was already standing when it arrived. It has watched more than five centuries of worshippers walk the approach since.

Eight hundred years is long enough to start leaning. By the early 2010s the trunk had tilted about ten degrees and the tree was in visible decline, and restoration work was carried out on it in April 2013. In October 2026 its crown was full and green.

It stands inside a low wooden fence in the front courtyard, a straw rope hung with paper streamers tied round the foot of the trunk and ferns growing on the bark. It is a day trip from Kagoshima: the train to Kirishima-Jingu station, then about fifteen minutes on the bus.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the one huge cedar inside a low wooden fence, with a straw rope and paper streamers round the foot of the trunk. It stands in the front courtyard, to the right of the approach to the main hall.

name: The Leaning Camphor of the Shiroyama Car Park

location.address: 新照院町, Kagoshima (car park below Shiroyama, about 250 m from kag_001)

access: Free; it stands at the edge of a public car park beside a small building, its main limb arching over the road and parking area. Visible from the car park.
transport: Near Shiroyama, same area as kag_001 (about 250 m); in Kagoshima city, local bus to Shiroyama. Stop name and time not checked.

photo_hint.own: Hidde photograph, sighting 1993a31d-f025-44d3-bcc1-6caa9cbba0eb, approved for use uncredited
photo_hint.open_licence: none found: Commons geosearch within 200 m returned only views from Shiroyama, no tree; iNaturalist has no camphor record within 120 m

recognise: A camphor with a massive trunk rising from a raised concrete bed beside a small building at the car park, its main limb leaning out and arching right across the road over the parked cars, fern-covered; kag_001 by contrast stands beside the walking path in the forest.
verify_notes: UNNAMED, ONE SOURCE ONLY: the owner's own photograph and phone GPS fix (31.5962204,130.5495004), approved for publication by Hidde 2026-10-02. Searched: Kagoshima city 保存樹 register (hozonju-02, 38 trees): no entry in 新照院町 (only a kuroganemochi in Terukuni Park for Shiroyama); several web searches on Shiroyama car park camphor found nothing naming it; Shiroyama is a national natural monument and historic site (1931) per kagoshima-kankou.com but that does not name this tree. No age, girth or height from any source; none estimated. Species camphor judged from the photograph (leaf, bark, form), not from a source. Pin is the owner's phone fix, honestly approximate (phone accuracy, tree beside the road); the photo shows the trunk base next to the small building so the viewing spot is right. ALIVE: owner photo 2026-10-02, full green crown. Whether the car park land is public: it is a car park, free per Kagoshima city park page for the Shiroyama park car park (城山公園駐車場, 城山町22-33, 37 spaces, free) but I did not confirm this is that exact car park. Page should ask the reader for girth and name. Ask: is a plaque at the base.
story:
Its main limb leaves the trunk at a slant and keeps going, out across the road, until it hangs over the cars parked on the other side. Almost everything else about this camphor is an open question.

Kagoshima keeps a register of 38 preserved trees, each measured and given a signboard at its foot. This one is not on it. It stands at the edge of a car park below Shiroyama, the hill above the city that has been a national natural monument and historic site since 1931, about 250 metres from the Camphor of Shiroyama on the forest path. Nothing written about Shiroyama mentions it.

What one visit shows: a massive trunk rising out of a raised concrete bed beside a small building, a crown that was full and green in October 2026, and ferns growing along the leaning limb. The species is read from the leaves, the bark and the shape of the tree rather than from any record, and nobody has published a name, a girth, a height or an age for it.

That makes it a tree you can help put on the record. If you are standing under it, a tape round the trunk at chest height would give it its first measurement. If there is a plaque at the base, or a name the neighbourhood uses for it, or you know when it was planted, tell us and this page will carry it.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the main limb, which leans out from a raised concrete bed beside a small building and arches right across the road over the parked cars. It stands at the car park's edge, not on the forest path.
